what_its_for: Bevacizumab-awwb is a cancer medicine used to treat several types of cancer, including colorectal cancer, lung cancer, kidney cancer, cervical cancer, ovarian cancer, and certain brain tumors (glioblastoma). It works by blocking a protein called VEGF that tumors need to grow new blood vessels. Without those blood vessels, the tumor cannot get the nutrients it needs to grow and spread.
how_to_take: This medicine is given through an IV (intravenous infusion) directly into your vein by a healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital setting. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Your first infusion may take about 90 minutes. If you tolerate it well, future infusions may be shortened to 60 minutes and then 30 minutes. Always let your nurse or doctor know right away if you feel unwell, dizzy, have chest pain, or have trouble breathing during the infusion.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your dose based on your body weight (measured in kilograms) and the type of cancer being treated. Doses typically range from 5 mg/kg to 15 mg/kg given every 2 or 3 weeks, depending on your treatment plan. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Never try to change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare professional, it is very unlikely you will miss a dose on your own. However, if you miss or need to reschedule an infusion appointment, call your doctor's office or cancer center as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not try to 'catch up' by doubling your dose. Your doctor will guide you on when your next infusion should happen.
storage: You do not need to store this medication at home. The clinic or hospital pharmacy handles storage. For your awareness: the unopened medicine vials must be kept in a refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). The vials must be kept in the original carton to protect them from light and should never be frozen or shaken.
what_to_avoid:
- Do NOT have any surgery, dental procedures, or invasive procedures without first telling your doctor you are on this medicine. Bevacizumab-awwb can slow wound healing and should be stopped at least 28 days before planned surgery.
- Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after your last dose.
- Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 6 months after your last dose.
- Tell all your doctors and dentists that you are receiving this medicine before any procedure.
- Avoid activities that increase bleeding risk if you have low platelet counts, such as contact sports or activities where you could get hurt.
when_to_call_doctor:
Call your doctor RIGHT AWAY or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following:
- Severe headache, confusion, vision changes, or seizures (signs of a rare but serious brain condition)
- Chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden numbness or weakness on one side (signs of a heart attack or stroke)
- Coughing up blood or vomiting blood
- Severe abdominal (belly) pain, cramping, or if you notice a hole or perforation in the gut
- A wound that is not healing properly or a wound that reopens
- Signs of severe infection: high fever, chills, redness, or swelling
- Sudden severe high blood pressure or vision problems
- Unusual swelling in your legs or signs of a blood clot
- Any infusion reaction symptoms during or after your infusion: hives, rash, itching, fever, chills, or trouble breathing
when_it_works: Bevacizumab-awwb starts working in your body right away at the cellular level, but you may not feel or see a difference immediately. It may take several weeks to months of treatment before your doctor can see results through scans or lab tests. Every person is different. Your doctor will monitor how well the treatment is working through regular check-ups, blood tests, and imaging scans throughout your treatment.
special_populations:
- PREGNANCY: This medicine can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after your last dose.
- BREASTFEEDING: Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least 6 months after your last dose, as the medicine may pass into breast milk and harm your baby.
- FERTILITY: This medicine may affect fertility in both men and women. Talk to your doctor before starting treatment if you plan to have children in the future.
- ELDERLY (age 65 and older): Older adults may have a higher risk of certain serious side effects, including blood clots, stroke, and heart problems. Your doctor will monitor you closely.
- CHILDREN: The safety and effectiveness of this medicine in children have not been fully established. It is primarily approved for use in adults.
- KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as this may affect how you respond to treatment.
